evidence: Cic. Att. 12.1.2: reliqua quae exspectābam ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī omnia
Verg. G. 2.490: fēlīx quī potuit rērum cognōscere causās
terms.comment: With an accusative or an accusative and infinitive, and ex or ab for the source: ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī is a stock phrase of Cicero’s letters. The perfect cognōvī means “I know”.

evidence: Ter. And. 211: Prīmum jam dē amōre hoc comperit
Caes. BG 1.22 (Lewis & Short): ut posteā ex captīvīs comperit
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to find out with certainty, to have or gain certain information”.

evidence: Caes. BG 1.11 (Lewis & Short): Caesarem certiōrem faciunt
terms.comment: Active aliquem certiōrem facere, to let someone know: fac mē certiōrem, “let me know” (Cic. Fam. 8.1.1, Caelius).

phrases.latin: reliqua quae exspectābam ex tuīs litterīs cognōvī omnia
phrases.english: Everything else I was waiting for I learned from your letter.

phrases.latin: sed sī tantus amor cāsūs cognōscere nostrōs … incipiam
phrases.english: But if you so long to learn what befell us … I will begin.
